subject: Human Evolution
title: The Multiregional Debate
description: A quick, practical guide to The Multiregional Debate.

hook.text: Did modern humans evolve once in Africa, or separately across multiple continents at the same time?

buildup.text: The multiregional hypothesis said Homo erectus evolved into Homo sapiens independently in Africa, Asia, and Europe.

discovery.text: DNA evidence decisively favored the Out of Africa model: one origin, then migration and mixing.

twist.text: But interbreeding with Neanderthals and Denisovans added a multiregional twist—genes did flow between regions.

climax.text: The truth is a blend: one main origin with significant genetic exchange along the way.

quiz.question: What did DNA evidence show about the multiregional hypothesis?
options: Refuted it but showed some interbreeding occurred
